current_criteria.name: visual_grounding
current_criteria.description: The answer must be directly supported by visible elements in the image. Annotators prefer answers that explicitly reference observable objects, positions, colors, or actions — and penalize those that make unsupported inferences or invent details not present in the image.

current_criteria.name: question_relevance
current_criteria.description: The answer must directly address the question without straying into irrelevant topics or adding extraneous information. Annotators prefer responses that focus on what is asked, even if the answer is negative or ambiguous — as long as it’s directly responsive.

current_criteria.name: factual_consistency_with_the_image
current_criteria.description: The answer must not contradict or misrepresent what is visibly present. Annotators penalize answers that misidentify objects, people, or actions — for example, claiming someone is taking a photo when the camera is idle, or mislabeling a bird species without visual evidence.

current_criteria.name: avoidance_of_hallucinated_visual_details
current_criteria.description: The answer must not invent or fabricate visual elements that are not present in the image. Annotators prefer cautious, evidence-based descriptions — even if they are vague — over confident claims that hallucinate details (e.g., ‘a red car is parked behind the building’ when none is visible).

current_criteria.name: calibrated_uncertainty
current_criteria.description: Annotators prefer answers that are cautious and honest when the visual evidence is ambiguous or insufficient. For example, saying ‘it is unclear what this object is’ is preferred over confidently asserting an unverifiable interpretation. This aligns with human preference for humility in the face of uncertainty.
